name: Duduela
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Greenhill, S. J. (ed.) transnewguinea.org / Lexibank transnewguineaorg: Uyajitaya lexicon (from Z'graggen 1980) and nine dialect lists (from Lambrecht et al. 2008); Didiwala list also credited to Rueck & Jore 2003 'The sociolinguistic situation of the Sam people' (SIL)
sources.note: Wordlists only, no stress marks, no prosodic notes.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Duduela does not occur in the 1971 volume (grep of the text layer hits only a table word 'nuru-'); not a source for this language.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record dudu1240 and reference records 43725, 27408, 156733, 108875, 302422, 701778
sources.note: Bibliographic only: 0 descriptive references; the remaining refs are Pawley 2005, Pawley & Hammarström 2017 (TNG classification) and Ethnologue 28.

sources.citation: SIL Global Publishing, Journal of Language Survey Reports index (13 pages) and entry 9137; SIL language/archive search pages for duk; pnglanguages.sil.org; PARADISEC items?language_code=duk; ELP lang/duk; OLAC language/duk
sources.note: The JLSR index lists exactly one SIL publication on [duk] (the 2008 survey report). SIL search pages, PARADISEC and ELP returned Cloudflare challenge pages (kept as receipts); OLAC was unreachable from our machine.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Duduela language' (redirect target of 'Uyajitaya language'), rev. 1 Jan 2026
ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2010. Change Request 2010-027 (Sara Van Cott, SIL-PNG, 2010-04-06; adopted 2011-05-18): reference name Duduela -> Uyajitaya.
sources.note: Nothing; naming and dialect record (Uyajitaya vs Amowe dialects), cites Lambrecht et al. 2008 as its only source; 'Nothing is known about the origin of the current name of the language, Duduela.'

sources.citation: Lambrecht, Philip, Alison Kassell, Margaret Potter & Sarah Tucker. 2008. The sociolinguistic situation of the Uyajitaya [duk] language. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2008-019. Dallas: SIL International. 46 pp. (survey 17-26 Nov 2003; text written Dec 2003)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 7.4 'Characteristics of the Language' (pp. 25-26) gives only consonant/vowel phone charts from the wordlist sessions, dialect alternations (p~ɸ~f, k~x~h, g~k, b~β, flap~trill) and SOV order; the strings stress/accent/tone/prosod/syllab do not occur anywhere in the 46 pages; Appendix E wordlist (pp. 41-45, nine village lists) carries no stress marks (page image p.41 checked). Sec. 11 p.32: 'There are no materials written in Uyajitaya.' Live sil.org PDF is Cloudflare-blocked; fetched sources via web.archive.org id_ copy (20241111130150).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-30. Canberra: ANU. xvi+181 pp. doi:10.15144/PL-D30
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 7 (pp. vii-viii): transcription 'rendered in a semiphonemic form, i.e. apparently non-contrastive phonetic details are omitted'; fluctuation table for Duduela (p~f, k-~h-, j~t, z~ž); no mention of stress. B20 Duduela entries carry vowel length but no stress marks (page image printed p.16 checked: 'agi- utu', 'mai'). Only prosodic remark in the volume is note 3 p.172 on Dumpu-Watiwa being tonal (a different language).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 569-612. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.8.2.2.1.1.5 (p.581): 'The Nuru Family consists of the languages Usu, Erima, Duduela, Kwato, Rerau, Jilim and Yangulam'; population, pronoun and lexical tables only; stress/accent/tone do not occur in the chapter's text layer.
